item.title: AI detects landslide risks years in advance using satellite radar data
item.description:
Around the village of Kimtang in central Nepal, cracks run through concrete steps and trees grow at odd angles — signs that the ground is shifting beneath residents' feet. Scientists at the University of Melbourne have used artificial intelligence to analyze satellite radar data and confirm what villagers long suspected: their homes sit atop an unstable slope at high risk of a devastating landslide. The AI marked the danger zone in bright red on a color map, a warning that could prove lifesaving.

The Nepal project is part of a growing wave of research applying AI to one of the world's most destructive and difficult-to-predict natural hazards. In the first two months of 2026 alone, 91 fatal landslides killed more than 800 people worldwide, according to data tracked by Eos. Researchers across multiple continents are now racing to deploy machine learning systems that can detect the subtle ground movements that precede catastrophic slope failures.

item.title: Gold surges as oil slump eases inflation fears
item.description:
Gold prices climbed sharply on Wednesday as a steep decline in oil prices eased inflation concerns and tempered expectations for interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve, even as mixed signals over a potential U.S.-Iran ceasefire kept markets on edge.

Spot gold rose nearly 2% to around $4,551 per ounce, while gold futures for April delivery jumped more than 3%, according to CNBC. The rally came as oil prices sank more than 5% on optimism that Washington was pursuing a diplomatic path to pause the conflict, with Brent crude falling to roughly $99 per barrel and West Texas Intermediate dropping to around $88.

item.title: Global stocks surge as US sends 15-point ceasefire plan to Iran
item.description:
Stock markets around the world rallied on Wednesday as investors reacted to reports that the United States had delivered a 15-point ceasefire proposal to Iran, raising hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the nearly month-old conflict that has roiled global markets and sent energy prices soaring.

The S&P 500 rose 1.1% in early trading, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed more than 500 points and the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.3%, according to the Associated Press. In Europe, Germany's DAX advanced 1.7%, France's CAC 40 climbed 1.4%, and Britain's FTSE 100 rose 0.9%. Asian markets posted even sharper gains, with Japan's Nikkei 225 surging nearly 3% and South Korea's Kospi jumping more than 3%. Oil prices fell sharply, with Brent crude dropping more than 5%.

item.title: NASA to send water-hunting tool to Moon aboard JAXA-ISRO rover
item.description: NASA announced it will provide a water-detecting instrument to the Lunar Polar Exploration mission, a joint effort by JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) and ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation) that aims to land a rover at the Moon's south pole no earlier than 2028.

item.title: Trump sets May 14-15 for rescheduled Beijing summit with Xi
item.description:
President Donald Trump will travel to Beijing on May 14 and 15 for a rescheduled summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping, the White House announced Wednesday, setting firm dates for a trip that had been thrown into uncertainty by the ongoing U.S. and Israeli war against Iran.

The visit was originally planned for March 31 to April 2 but was postponed as Trump said he needed to remain in Washington to oversee military operations, known as Operation Epic Fury. The announcement comes even as the conflict in Iran continues and the administration presses Tehran to accept a ceasefire proposal.

item.title: Iran signals preference for Vance as US negotiator, rejecting Witkoff and Kushner
item.description:
Iran has signaled to the Trump administration that it prefers to negotiate with Vice President JD Vance rather than other senior officials, rejecting renewed engagement with special envoy Steve Witkoff and presidential son-in-law Jared Kushner, according to a CNN report citing two regional sources.

The message was conveyed through back channels to mediating countries, with Iranian representatives expressing that talks involving Witkoff and Kushner would not be productive given what sources described as a "deficit of trust". The collapse of earlier nuclear negotiations in Geneva, followed within days by US and Israeli military strikes that began on February 28, left Tehran deeply skeptical of the pair's intentions.

item.title: Iran rejects U.S. ceasefire plan, issues five demands
item.description: Iran on Wednesday dismissed a 15-point American proposal to end the nearly month-long war in the Middle East, with Tehran issuing its own set of demands and mocking Washington's diplomatic efforts as detached from reality. The rejection came as fighting between Iran on one side and the United States and Israel on the other showed no signs of abating.

item.title: U.N. report finds migratory freshwater fish declined 81% since 1970
item.description: Migratory freshwater fish populations have declined by 81 percent worldwide since 1970, according to a new United Nations assessment that calls the crisis one of the steepest drops recorded for any major vertebrate group. The report, released this week at the CMS COP15 wildlife conference in Campo Grande, Brazil, identifies 325 species in urgent need of coordinated international conservation action.

item.title: 20-year study finds mammal cloning hits fatal genetic wall after 58 generations
item.description: A landmark 20-year experiment has revealed that mammals cannot be cloned indefinitely, overturning earlier assumptions and dimming hopes that the technology could one day be used to preserve endangered species or mass-produce livestock without limit.

item.title: Trump rebuffed Netanyahu's push to call for Iranian uprising
item.description:
President Trump rebuffed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's proposal to jointly call on Iranians to take to the streets and overthrow their government, telling Netanyahu during a phone call last week that protesters would "get mowed down," according to Axios.

"Why the hell should we tell people to take to the streets when they'll just get mowed down," Trump told Netanyahu during the call, according to a U.S. official. Netanyahu had argued that the Iranian regime was in disarray and that the moment presented an opportunity for further destabilization. Trump disagreed, reflecting a position he has voiced publicly — that Iran's security forces make civilian uprising nearly impossible.

item.title: Iran bolsters defenses on Kharg Island ahead of possible US assault
item.description:
Iran has been laying traps, moving additional military personnel, and deploying air defense systems to Kharg Island in recent weeks as it braces for a potential US operation to seize the strategic oil hub, according to CNN, citing multiple people familiar with US intelligence reporting.

The buildup comes as the Trump administration weighs whether to use ground forces to take control of the tiny island in the northeastern Persian Gulf, which handles roughly 90% of Iran's crude exports, as leverage to force Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Egypt offers to host Iran-US talks as Tehran rejects ceasefire plan
item.description:
Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty announced on Wednesday that Cairo stands ready to host negotiations between Washington and Tehran, describing a direct meeting between the two sides as potentially "the last opportunity to avoid a fully fledged escalation in the region."

"We have to continue our efforts, it's all about diplomacy and negotiations," Abdelatty said at a press conference in Cairo, where he voiced support for President Donald Trump's initiative to negotiate with Iran. The offer came on the same day that Iran formally rejected a 15-point US ceasefire proposal delivered through Pakistan, with Iranian officials dismissing the plan and issuing their own counterdemands.

item.title: Iranian analyst warns Tehran ready to seize UAE, Bahrain coastlines
item.description: An Iranian national security analyst declared on state television that Tehran's armed forces are prepared to capture the coastlines of Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates if the United States "makes any mistake" in the region, ratcheting up threats against Gulf neighbors already under sustained aerial bombardment since the war began on February 28.

item.title: Israel hits Tehran naval research center, completes waves of strikes
item.description: As the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran enters its 26th day, Israel is escalating its air campaign across Iran even as President Donald Trump signals that diplomatic talks to end the conflict are advancing. The Israeli military completed multiple waves of large-scale strikes targeting government infrastructure in Tehran and a submarine development facility in Isfahan on Tuesday and Wednesday, while Iran continued retaliatory missile barrages against Israeli cities.

item.title: US and Israel temporarily spare two Iranian leaders to allow peace talks
item.description: The United States and Israel have temporarily removed two senior Iranian officials from their elimination lists to create a window for potential peace negotiations, even as military operations in Iran continue nearly a month into the conflict.

item.title: Iran says it now controls Strait of Hormuz transit rules permanently
item.description:
Iran's military declared Wednesday that it has permanently rewritten the rules of passage through the Strait of Hormuz, asserting sole authority over who may transit the waterway that carries roughly one-fifth of the world's oil supply.

"The situation in the strait will not return to the past," said Ebrahim Zolfaghari, spokesperson for the Iranian military's Khatam Al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, in remarks carried by Iran's Mehr News Agency. "Permission for transit will be determined by us."

Zolfaghari added that "the fire beneath oil prices has been ignited, and its level is in our hands," framing energy markets as a weapon in Iran's confrontation with the United States and Israel, whose joint bombing campaign against Iran began on February 28.

item.title: Iran rejects U.S. ceasefire plan as war nears one-month mark
item.description: Nearly a month after the United States and Israel launched coordinated military strikes on Iran on February 28, the conflict shows no signs of abating — and its economic toll is mounting. Iran on Wednesday rejected a U.S. ceasefire proposal and laid out its own conditions for ending the war, even as oil prices remained volatile and economists warned of growing recession risks worldwide.

item.title: 20-year study finds mammal cloning fails after 58 generations
item.description:
Mammals cannot be cloned indefinitely. That is the conclusion of a 20-year experiment in Japan, where researchers serially cloned mice across 58 generations only to watch the final generation die within a day of birth — victims of what scientists describe as a "mutational meltdown."

The study, published March 24 in Nature Communications, establishes for the first time a hard ceiling on mammalian cloning and underscores the irreplaceable role of sexual reproduction in maintaining genetic health.

item.title: Mullally installed as first female Archbishop of Canterbury
item.description: Dame Sarah Mullally was installed Wednesday as the 106th Archbishop of Canterbury at a ceremony in Canterbury Cathedral, becoming the first woman to hold the office in its nearly 1,500-year history and assuming spiritual leadership of 85 million Anglicans worldwide.

item.title: Zelensky says US tied security guarantees to Ukraine ceding Donbas
item.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky disclosed on Wednesday that the United States has made its offer of security guarantees for a peace deal conditional on Kyiv withdrawing from the entire Donbas region in eastern Ukraine, a demand he warned would undermine the security of both Ukraine and Europe.

"The Americans are prepared to finalise these guarantees at a high level once Ukraine is ready to withdraw from Donbas," Zelensky told Reuters in an exclusive interview conducted at the presidential compound in Kyiv. He cautioned that such a withdrawal would cede the region's heavily fortified defensive positions to Russia, weakening Ukraine's ability to deter future aggression.
